projects.title: Lucid SOC
projects.tagline: Autonomous LangGraph AI Analyst with Transparent Glass-Box Reasoning
projects.short: LangGraph AI analyst that investigates alerts, queries the SIEM, enriches IoCs and isolates hosts. Every thought is logged. Isolated live Lumma Stealer in 4 seconds.
projects.why: Security Operations Centers drown in repetitive alerts, leading to alert fatigue and delayed incident response. Traditional playbooks lack autonomous multi-hop reasoning, while black-box LLMs cannot be audited.
projects.what: Architected an asynchronous event-driven SOAR/triage platform in Python and FastAPI. Implemented a LangGraph ReAct agent powered by Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite with glass-box transparency, serializing Thoughts, Actions, and Observations. Integrated with Wazuh SIEM, OpenSearch DSL queries, VirusTotal/AbuseIPDB caching, and automatic host containment via Wazuh REST API.
projects.outcome: Validated on live Lumma Stealer malware execution: correlated Suricata TLS SNI with Sysmon Event ID 3 network sockets and executed automated host isolation in 4 seconds.
projects.architecture: Event ingestion via Filebeat into Wazuh & OpenSearch -> Asynchronous FastAPI backend -> LangGraph ReAct Agent -> Contextual IoC Enrichment with SQLite caching -> Automated Wazuh REST API active response endpoint isolation.
highlights: Glass-box explainability logging every LLM reasoning step for Tier-3 SOC auditing
Sub-second alert correlation across Suricata network telemetry and Sysmon process events
Automated active containment triggering Wazuh agent endpoint isolation in 4 seconds
Deterministic pre-LLM noise filtering preventing unnecessary token usage

projects.title: Anomaly Engine
projects.tagline: Unsupervised Behavioral Analytics with Drain3 Log Parsing & SHAP Explainability
projects.short: Isolation Forest on streaming log templates, SHAP explanations, and a Mark-as-Normal feedback loop.
projects.why: Static detection rules consistently miss novel zero-day attack patterns and unknown anomalous behavior, while standard machine learning models produce unexplainable black-box alarms that analysts ignore.
projects.what: Containerized a continuous 5-minute unsupervised inference daemon with zero-downtime hot-reloading. Applied Drain3 streaming template mining to convert raw logs into frequency vectors, trained an Isolation Forest (IForest) with synthetic outlier injection, and integrated SHAP TreeExplainer for feature attribution.
projects.outcome: Analysts can inspect mathematical feature contributions for any anomaly score above 75. Clicking 'Mark as Normal' duplicates benign vectors 50x in scheduled retraining to permanently eliminate recurring false positives.
projects.architecture: Raw Wazuh archives -> Drain3 semantic log clustering -> 5-min sliding window vectorization -> PyOD Isolation Forest -> ECDF 0-100 score calibration -> SHAP TreeExplainer -> Closed-loop feedback retraining.
highlights: Drain3 streaming log template mining strips dynamic variables (IPs, paths, GUIDs)
Empirical Cumulative Distribution Function (ECDF) score calibration to intuitive 0-100 percentiles
SHAP explainability translating feature vectors back into human-readable log templates
Human-in-the-loop retraining mechanism shifting decision trees to suppress false positives

projects.title: Zero-Trust Lab
projects.tagline: Cloud-Native Gartner SASE / Zero Trust Architecture with 0 Inbound Attack Surface
projects.short: AWS EC2 with 0 inbound rules behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, Entra ID identity and device posture checks.
projects.why: Traditional perimeter firewalls and legacy VPNs grant broad network-level trust once authenticated, exposing enterprises to lateral movement and public port reconnaissance.
projects.what: Deployed an AWS EC2 Ubuntu production server with zero inbound firewall rules. Routed all access through an outbound-only Cloudflare Tunnel (`cloudflared`). Integrated Microsoft Entra ID as the IdP and configured Cloudflare WARP client posture checks, agentless browser-rendered SSH, Secure Web Gateway (SWG) DNS filtering, and GitHub SaaS API CASB audits.
projects.outcome: Eliminated 100% of exposed network ports against external port scanners while enforcing granular identity, MFA, and device health posture before granting micro-segmented application access.
projects.architecture: User Device (Cloudflare WARP Posture) -> Microsoft Entra ID (SAML/OIDC MFA) -> Cloudflare Edge & SWG -> Outbound Cloudflare Tunnel -> AWS EC2 (0 Inbound Security Group Rules).
highlights: Zero inbound Security Group rules completely neutralizing external port scans and shodan discovery
Outbound-only bidirectional encrypted TLS tunnel brokering web and administrative traffic
Browser-rendered SSH gateway eliminating the need for exposed bastion hosts or SSH keys on endpoints
Automated SaaS CASB integration scanning GitHub repositories for posture drift

projects.title: Purple Team AD Lab
projects.tagline: Adversary Emulation in Active Directory Defended with Wazuh, Suricata & Sysmon
projects.short: BadBlood-populated Active Directory attacked with Atomic Red Team, defended with Wazuh, Suricata, Zeek and Sysmon.
projects.why: Security detection rules require a realistic, enterprise-scale Active Directory environment with messy background telemetry to properly tune high-fidelity detections and eliminate false positives.
projects.what: Constructed a multi-subnet virtualized enterprise lab isolated via pfSense router (WAN, LAN, DMZ). Populated Windows Server Active Directory with BadBlood (generating hundreds of users, groups, and ACLs). Executed MITRE ATT&CK test cases via Atomic Red Team and engineered multi-layer detections across Wazuh SIEM, Suricata NIDS, Zeek, and Sysmon.
projects.outcome: Engineered custom detection rules and behavioral signatures mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, achieving high-confidence detection of Kerberoasting, Pass-the-Hash, and scheduled task persistence.
projects.architecture: pfSense segmented hypervisor lab -> Windows Domain Controller (Sysmon v13 + BadBlood) -> Kali Linux Attack Node (Atomic Red Team) -> Syslog-ng -> Wazuh Manager & Suricata NIDS.
highlights: Automated BadBlood synthesis providing enterprise-like Active Directory complexity
Multi-layer defense telemetry fusing network packet inspection with kernel-level process events
Sysmon configuration specifically tuned for Event IDs 1, 3, 11, and 13
Continuous Purple Teaming feedback loop translating red team tradecraft into blue team rules

projects.title: Responsible Disclosure
projects.tagline: Client-Side Validation Bypass (CWE-602) Discovery & Remediation on Rosetta Stone
projects.short: GraphQL client-side validation bypass (CWE-602), exploited with Burp rules, 9-page report with fixes.
projects.why: Web applications that delegate authorization and test-evaluation logic to the client browser enable malicious actors to manipulate grades and bypass access controls.
projects.what: Conducted independent security research on the Rosetta Stone Fluency Builder platform. Discovered CWE-602 vulnerability where client-side React code transmitted test answers and score calculations to the GraphQL backend. Engineered Burp Suite Match & Replace regex rules demonstrating zero-touch automated score manipulation and authored a 9-page responsible disclosure report with remediation guidance.
projects.outcome: Documented full vulnerability chain, risk assessment, and server-side verification code patches; safely submitted to vendor via responsible disclosure.
projects.architecture: React Client UI -> Intercepted GraphQL Mutations -> Burp Suite Match & Replace automation -> Backend Rosetta Stone GraphQL API -> CWE-602 Exploitation Demonstration.
highlights: In-depth reverse engineering of client-side JavaScript score computation logic
Custom Burp Suite automation rules enabling reliable, non-destructive proof-of-concept validation
Comprehensive 9-page vulnerability report detailing threat impact, CVSS score, and server-side fixes
Adherence to ethical hacking standards and responsible disclosure best practices

projects.title: Smart TV Red Team
projects.tagline: IoT Attack Chain: Exposed ADB to Root Access, LAN Pivoting & Session Hijacking
projects.short: Exposed ADB to root shell, LAN pivot and session-token theft showing 2FA bypass.
projects.why: Unsecured smart devices inside internal networks provide low-effort entry points for attackers to establish persistence and pivot into corporate or private subnets.
projects.what: Discovered open Android Debug Bridge (ADB port 5555) on a target Smart TV during lab vulnerability scanning. Obtained root privileges, extracted cleartext Wi-Fi pre-shared keys, queried SQLite databases to harvest active OAuth/session tokens (bypassing 2FA), tapped the hardware microphone via HAL, and deployed an automated persistence APK.
projects.outcome: Demonstrated the full attack blast radius from a single smart device compromise, authored hardening recommendations, and published an educational write-up.
projects.architecture: Nmap subnet discovery -> TCP 5555 ADB Exploitation -> Root privilege escalation -> SQLite credential extraction -> Hardware abstraction layer audio tapping -> Subnet pivoting.
highlights: Complete chain from unauthenticated network probe to root system shell
Session hijacking demonstrating 2FA circumvention via direct cookie/token theft
Hardware abstraction layer manipulation accessing onboard audio microphone
Prescriptive mitigation strategies for IoT segmentation and firmware hardening

projects.title: AWS Secrets Monitor
projects.tagline: Event-Driven Serverless Detection & Alerting Pipeline for Cloud Secrets Access
projects.short: CloudTrail to CloudWatch to SNS alerting on suspicious secret access.
projects.why: Privileged credentials stored in cloud key vaults are primary targets; unauthorized access must be detected and alerted within seconds to prevent data breaches.
projects.what: Engineered an event-driven AWS security monitoring pipeline. Captured all AWS Secrets Manager API calls through multi-region AWS CloudTrail, ingested events into CloudWatch Log Groups with metric filter patterns, and triggered immediate SNS alerting upon abnormal secret retrieval.
projects.outcome: Configured automated real-time notification pipeline with immutable audit logs stored in an S3 bucket with Object Lock for forensic non-repudiation.
projects.architecture: AWS Secrets Manager API -> AWS CloudTrail Multi-Region Trail -> S3 Immutable Audit Vault -> CloudWatch Log Filter -> CloudWatch Alarm -> Amazon SNS Alert -> Security Team Email.
highlights: Zero-latency alerting on sensitive GetSecretValue API calls
Immutable audit trails protected with S3 Object Lock and strict bucket policies
Least-privilege IAM policies and KMS key access scoping
Scalable serverless design with zero infrastructure maintenance overhead

projects.title: Cyberlaw Study
projects.tagline: Comparative Regulatory Framework: Moroccan Law 05-20, Law 09-08, LPM & EU GDPR
projects.short: Moroccan Law 05-20 and 09-08, French law and GDPR mapped to technical controls.
projects.what: Authored an academic and technical comparative analysis mapping Moroccan cybersecurity and privacy legislation (Law 05-20, Law 09-08) alongside European counterparts (EU GDPR, French LPM). Established matrix translating legal obligations into tangible technical security controls.
projects.outcome: Produced a complete mapping matrix connecting statutory data breach notification, mandatory cryptography, log retention, and Data Protection Officer responsibilities directly to SIEM, IAM, and DLP configurations.

Cross-jurisdictional comparison between Moroccan and European regulatory frameworks
Practical playbook for compliance auditing, incident disclosure timelines, and data subject rights
Foundation for enterprise security governance and risk management compliance

projects.title: AI-Augmented DevSecOps & Secure Payment
projects.tagline: Automated Cloud CI/CD DevSecOps Pipeline with OWASP Defense & Sandbox Banking Security
projects.short: Under Development · Cloud DevSecOps pipeline automating 11 Tier-1 practices with SAST/DAST/SCA/Secrets scanning and a hardened payment sandbox.
projects.why: Modern rapid software delivery requires continuous security embedded directly into developer workflows (Shift-Left) without manual bottlenecks, while payment platforms face severe threats of transaction tampering, replay attacks, and sensitive cardholder data exposure.
projects.what: Currently in active development for the 'Sécurité des applications et des services' module at FST Marrakech. Engineering a cloud-deployable architecture encompassing Web front-end, Mobile app, REST/GraphQL APIs, and microservices backend. Automating all 11 Tier 1 DevSecOps security practices (Prates & Pereira framework) and advanced Tier 2 resilience mechanisms in CI/CD, incorporating SAST, DAST, SCA, and Secret Scanning for both human and AI-generated code. Developing and securing a simulated bank card payment system in a sandbox environment with active countermeasures against transaction manipulation, replay attacks, and token theft.
projects.outcome: Targeting 100% automated gate enforcement blocking vulnerable code and leaked secrets prior to deployment, while securing payment workflows against OWASP Top 10 Web (2025), Mobile, API, and LLM vulnerabilities.
projects.architecture: Code Commit (Git/GitLab) -> Automated Pre-Commit & Secret Scanning -> CI/CD Pipeline (SAST + SCA Dependency Check) -> Dynamic Testing (DAST) -> Hardened Container Deployment -> Sandboxed Payment Gateway (Replay & Tamper Defenses) -> Threat Modeling & Auditing.

Automating all 11 Tier 1 DevSecOps security practices within cloud CI/CD pipelines
Integrating SAST, DAST, SCA, and Secret Scanning auditing human and AI-generated contributions
Hardened bank card payment sandbox with cryptographic protection against transaction replay and tampering
Comprehensive threat modeling across OWASP Top 10 Web (2025), Mobile, API, and LLM Applications

projects.title: Signal E2EE Protocol
projects.tagline: Cryptographic Analysis & Implementation: X3DH, Double Ratchet & Authenticated Encryption
projects.short: Mathematical modeling and implementation of the Signal Protocol (X3DH, Double Ratchet, AES-256-CBC, HMAC-SHA256) proving Forward Secrecy & Post-Compromise Security.
projects.why: Modern end-to-end encrypted messaging requires mathematical guarantees that compromised ephemeral keys or long-term identities cannot expose past communications (Forward Secrecy) or future messages (Post-Compromise Security).
projects.what: Conducted an in-depth mathematical analysis and implementation study of the Signal Protocol at FST Marrakech. Modeled the Extended Triple Diffie-Hellman (X3DH) asynchronous handshake using Identity Keys, Signed Prekeys, Ephemeral Keys, and One-Time Prekeys to derive a shared 256-bit root key via 4 ECDH operations. Built the Double Ratchet state machine combining Symmetric-key KDF Ratchets for per-message forward secrecy with Diffie-Hellman Ratchets for post-compromise self-healing. Implemented Authenticated Encryption (AE) pairing AES-256-CBC with HMAC-SHA256.
projects.outcome: Mathematically verified zero past message recovery upon endpoint compromise through ephemeral message key deletion, and guaranteed future recovery through active DH ratchet advancement on each conversational round-trip.
projects.architecture: Session Init: X3DH (Identity Keys + Signed Prekey + One-Time Prekey) -> 256-bit Root Key derivation via 4x ECDH -> Double Ratchet (DH Ratchet + Symmetric KDF Ratchet) -> Message Encryption: AES-256-CBC (128-bit IV) + HMAC-SHA256.
highlights: Extended Triple Diffie-Hellman (X3DH) modeling asynchronous session setup with 4 ECDH operations
Double Ratchet state machine combining symmetric KDF chains with asymmetric DH ratchets
Mathematical proof and enforcement of Forward Secrecy and Post-Compromise Security
Authenticated Encryption construction pairing AES-256-CBC with HMAC-SHA256 integrity checks

projects.short: Handcrafted in the pre-AI era: 100% manually coded from scratch. Centralizes team task management, code version control, and real-time messaging.
projects.why: Student and engineering teams struggle with fragmented tooling across task boards, chat applications, and code repositories. Building an all-in-one platform without modern AI code assistants required complete mastery of full-stack system architecture, data models, and network protocols from first principles.
projects.what: Architected and engineered UniCollab entirely in the pre-AI era, manually coded from scratch line by line with zero AI assistance. Built a complete full-stack web application featuring interactive Kanban task management, a custom lightweight code version control system for tracking project source files, low-latency multi-user WebSocket real-time messaging, and synchronized team collaboration.
projects.outcome: Demonstrated strong software engineering and architectural rigor by crafting complex client-side reactivity, backend APIs, WebSocket pub/sub synchronization, and database schemas entirely by hand with clean, maintainable code.
projects.architecture: Client Web Application -> REST & WebSocket APIs -> Custom Task & Workflow Engine -> Lightweight Source File Revision Store -> Real-Time Message Broker -> Relational Database.
highlights: Built in the pre-AI era: 100% manually coded from scratch with zero AI coding assistance
Interactive Kanban task board with custom drag-and-drop state transitions and progress analytics
Custom-built lightweight code version control system tracking multi-file project revisions
Full-duplex real-time WebSocket messaging and live multi-user team synchronization
